title: The finite-stage boundary input is a consequence
statement:
The boundary duality input of [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]
holds for every separated finite-type $Y/k$ and every finite stage
$A=A_{E,n}$. In particular the canonical evaluation-defined map

$$
\beta_L:i^*D_TL\longrightarrow D_ZRi^!L
$$

is an isomorphism for every closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$
between the locally closed pieces in that definition.

proof.text: Work first on the small etale sites with the finite constant ring $A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $Y$ is Noetherian. Write a locally closed piece as a closed subscheme of an open $V\subseteq Y$. The open is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], so its inclusion is quasi-compact and hence finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. The closed inclusion is proper and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Composing finite generating sets on affine charts proves finite type of the piece over $k$; its diagonal is the restriction of the closed diagonal of $Y/k$, hence it is separated. The Noetherian lemma applies again. By [thm-fix-general-biduality], $\omega_T=Ra_T^!A$ is defined and $D_T$ preserves the required finite-Tor constructible domain, and $\delta_L:L\to D_TD_TL$ is an isomorphism. This proves preservation for every piece. Nagata [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies compactifications of the structure maps. For a closed $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$, use its proper compactification with identity open part: [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $Ri_!=Ri_*$. Their etale ambient right adjoints exist by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. In taking composition mates, use the bounded-below restrictions: [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] gives the right adjoints on the bounded-below comparison class, and [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] specifies these as the transported etale adjoints. The equivalence with the etale bounded-below category follows from [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]; the left-adjoint identification is [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Each compactification is finite type over $k$, so [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound], applied over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, supplies the finite dimension bound needed for that class theorem. Now apply the actual etale $D^+$ composition isomorphism of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] and [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition], evaluated at $A$. Since $a_Z=a_Ti$, they give $Ri^!\omega_T\cong\omega_Z$, with the pasted counits. All inputs to these restricted adjunctions are bounded below. No unbounded pro-etale adjunction or unbounded compact-support composition theorem is used.

source.place: First paragraph: preservation and the dualizing-object identification needed for alpha

proof.text:
Fix $L\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ and put $P=i^*D_TL$ and $U=Ri^!L$. The etale $i^*$ is the exact constant-coefficient inverse image by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; [prop-constructible-pullback] therefore makes $P$ bounded constructible. For its Tor bound, use [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] to send $D_TL$ to the finite-Tor pro-etale category, apply [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] there, and identify its result with $\nu_Z^*P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. The converse clause of [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] reflects that bound to the bounded etale complex $P$. Thus $P\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ with no silent identification of the two sites. Apply [lem-weil-closed-costalk-duality] to $D_TL$. It gives an isomorphism $\widetilde\alpha_{D_TL}:Ri^!D_TD_TL\to D_ZP$. Thus
$$\widetilde c_L=\widetilde\alpha_{D_TL}\circ Ri^!\delta_L:U\xrightarrow{\sim}D_ZP.$$
Consequently $U$ is finite-Tor constructible, because $D_ZP$ is so by [thm-fix-general-biduality]. The same argument applied to any $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$ shows $Ri^!K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$, in particular for $K=D_TL$. This conclusion used costalk duality and biduality, without using the boundary exchange. Here the tildes distinguish a preservation witness from the evaluation-normalized comparison to be constructed in step 4; no normalization of the costalk lemma is inferred from its statement.

source.place: First paragraph: alpha composed with the double-dual map and the finite-Tor domain

proof.text:
Record the tensor--internal-Hom adjunction used in the remaining map calculations on the actual ringed sites. Given $B,C,H\in D(A_W)$, choose a K-flat flat-term representative $Q$ of $C$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and a K-injective representative $I$ of $H$ by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective] show that $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(Q,I)$ is a K-injective representative of $R\mathcal Hom(C,H)$. The natural complex isomorphism [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] identifies the representatives of $R\mathcal Hom(B,R\mathcal Hom(C,H))$ and $R\mathcal Hom(B\otimes^LC,H)$. Taking $H^0$ of derived global sections and applying [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(B,R\mathcal Hom(C,H))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B\otimes^LC,H).$$
The counit is evaluation; transposition is natural in all three variables. This proves the needed adjunction from statements about small ringed sites, rather than citing an adjunction for $\mathcal O_X$-modules as though it were an adjunction for etale $A$-modules. Tensor symmetry is the signed interchange of homogeneous factors, $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{\deg x\deg y}y\otimes x$; the two interchanges compose to the identity and respect the total differential.

Write $\mu_N:Ri_!Ri^!N\to N$ for the exceptional counit. For finite-Tor constructible $M,N$ on $T$, define
$$q_{M,N}:i^*M\otimes^LRi^!N\longrightarrow Ri^!(M\otimes^LN)$$
to be its exceptional-adjunction transpose of
$$Ri_!(i^*M\otimes^LRi^!N)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}^{-1}} M\otimes^LRi_!Ri^!N\xrightarrow{1\otimes\mu_N}M\otimes^LN.$$
Here [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula] applies: $M$ is finite-Tor constructible and $Ri^!N$ is bounded constructible by step 2; swapping factors gives the displayed order. The exceptional adjunction is [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Naturality of the projection map and counit gives naturality of $q$ in $M,N$. Define
$$r_K=Ri^!(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma_{K,D_TK})\circ q_{K,D_TK}\circ\sigma_{Ri^!D_TK,i^*K}:Ri^!D_TK\otimes^Li^*K\longrightarrow\omega_Z.$$
This fixes the normalization of the comparison $\alpha_K$ as the tensor--Hom transpose of $r_K$. To verify it independently of the proof of the costalk node, for $B\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ the adjunctions of step 3 and the exceptional adjunction, followed by the projection isomorphism, give
$$\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B,Ri^!D_TK)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(Ri_!B\otimes^LK,\omega_T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_T(Ri_!(B\otimes^Li^*K),\omega_T)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_Z(B,D_Zi^*K).$$
The first and last functors in $B$ are represented by objects of $D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$ by steps 1--2; the intermediate Hom sets are taken in the ambient category on $T$. The Yoneda bijection [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful], applied to that full category, turns this chain into an isomorphism. Evaluating the chain at $B=Ri^!D_TK$ and its identity gives exactly the displayed $r_K$, since the exceptional transpose of the identity is $\mu_{D_TK}$. Thus the canonical evaluation-normalized comparison is an isomorphism, as required for the $\alpha$ of [lem-weil-closed-costalk-duality]. This explicit calculation does not take an evaluation characterization from that node's proof. From this point onward let $\alpha_K$ denote this constructed normalized isomorphism, and set $c_L=\alpha_{D_TL}\circ Ri^!\delta_L$. Both factors are isomorphisms, so $c_L$ is an isomorphism. The preliminary $\widetilde c_L$ served only to establish the domain in step 2.

source.place: Second paragraph: make the adjunction/evaluation normalization of the costalk comparison explicit

proof.text:
By [lem-weil-duality-pairing], $\delta_L$ is the transpose of evaluation after tensor symmetry. The defining transpose equation is therefore
$$\mathrm{ev}_{D_TL}\circ(\delta_L\otimes1_{D_TL})=\mathrm{ev}_L\circ\sigma_{L,D_TL}.$$
This is an equality of maps $L\otimes^LD_TL\to\omega_T$, with the same signed symmetry as in step 3. No invertibility is needed for this identity.

source.place: Second paragraph: the evaluation identity used to identify the canonical boundary map

proof.text:
Let
$$b_L=Ri^!\mathrm{ev}_L\circ q_{D_TL,L}:P\otimes^LU\longrightarrow\omega_Z.$$
This is the pairing whose transpose defines $\beta_L$ in [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]. Let $t(c_L)=\mathrm{ev}_P\circ(c_L\otimes1_P)$ be the transpose of $c_L$. The formula for $r$ in step 4, naturality of $q$ in its second variable, naturality of tensor symmetry, and step 5 give the following equality of maps $U\otimes^LP\to\omega_Z$:
$$\begin{aligned}
t(c_L)&=r_{D_TL}\circ(Ri^!\delta_L\otimes1_P)\\
&=Ri^!\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_{D_TL}\circ\sigma_{D_TL,D_TD_TL}\circ(1_{D_TL}\otimes\delta_L)\bigr)\circ q_{D_TL,L}\circ\sigma_{U,P}\\
&=Ri^!\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_{D_TL}\circ(\delta_L\otimes1_{D_TL})\circ\sigma_{D_TL,L}\bigr)\circ q_{D_TL,L}\circ\sigma_{U,P}\\
&=Ri^!\bigl(\mathrm{ev}_L\circ\sigma_{L,D_TL}\circ\sigma_{D_TL,L}\bigr)\circ q_{D_TL,L}\circ\sigma_{U,P}\\
&=b_L\circ\sigma_{U,P}.
\end{aligned}$$
The last line uses $\sigma_{L,D_TL}\sigma_{D_TL,L}=1$. Thus $c_L$ and $\beta_L$ are the two currying maps of this same pairing, in opposite tensor orders.

source.place: Second paragraph: identify the transpose of alpha composed with Ri! delta

proof.text:
Naturality of evaluation for $c_L:U\to D_ZP$ gives
$$\mathrm{ev}_U\circ(D_Zc_L\otimes1_U)=\mathrm{ev}_{D_ZP}\circ(1_{D_ZD_ZP}\otimes c_L).$$
Precomposing with $\delta_P\otimes1_U$ and using the transpose identity from step 5 on $Z$ shows that the transpose of $D_Z(c_L)\circ\delta_P$ is $b_L$. Uniqueness under the adjunction of step 3 therefore gives the specified-map identity
$$\beta_L=D_Z(c_L)\circ\delta_P.$$
Both factors are isomorphisms: $c_L$ is an isomorphism by step 4, a functor sends its inverse to an inverse, and $\delta_P$ is an isomorphism by [thm-fix-general-biduality], since $P\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,A)$. Hence the canonical evaluation-defined boundary map is an isomorphism.

source.place: First displayed double-duality composite and second paragraph: its inverse is the canonical beta

proof.text:
For the evaluation compatibility, fix $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. The transpose of $\beta_{D_TK}\circ i^*\delta_K$ is
$$Ri^!\mathrm{ev}_{D_TK}\circ q_{D_TD_TK,D_TK}\circ(i^*\delta_K\otimes1_{Ri^!D_TK}).$$
Naturality of $q$ and step 5 rewrite this as
$$Ri^!(\mathrm{ev}_K\circ\sigma_{K,D_TK})\circ q_{K,D_TK}:i^*K\otimes^LRi^!D_TK\longrightarrow\omega_Z.$$
On the other hand the transpose of $D_Z(\alpha_K)\circ\delta_{i^*K}$ is $r_K\circ\sigma_{i^*K,Ri^!D_TK}$, by naturality of evaluation and the defining transpose of $\delta_{i^*K}$. This is the very same displayed map, by the formula for $r_K$ in step 4. Uniqueness of transposition yields
$$\beta_{D_TK}\circ i^*\delta_K=D_Z(\alpha_K)\circ\delta_{i^*K}.$$
Composing with $(D_Z\alpha_K)^{-1}$ gives exactly the double-dual compatibility required in [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]. The two cancellations of symmetry use its involutivity, so they include the Koszul signs.

source.place: Second paragraph: explicit equation for compatibility with the restricted double-dual morphism

proof.text:
Finally consider the small pro-etale realization of [def-weil-boundary-duality-input]. Fix its same global datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, so $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. The pieces $T,Z$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes by step 1. Put $C_W=\nu_W^*$ and $F_e=Ri^{\mathrm{et}}_!$, $F_p=Ri^{\mathrm{proet}}_!$. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] every bounded constructible input is $C_TK$ for an etale bounded constructible $K$, and [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude] reflects and preserves finite Tor amplitude. Ordinary restriction agrees by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Exceptional restriction is the specified functor $C_Zi^\times R\nu_{T,*}$ of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], whose value on $C_TK$ is $C_Zi^\times K$ by the unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. Use the identity-open compactification of $i$ in [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], so $F_e=Ri_{\mathrm{et},*}$ and $F_p=Ri_{\mathrm{proet},*}$. Write $\eta_B:F_pC_ZB\xrightarrow{\sim}C_TF_eB$ for the inverse of the named comparison $b_{i,B}$ in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. This specifies the proper-case compact-support comparison, including its normalization. On etale-origin objects the transported exceptional adjunction is the explicit chain
$$\operatorname{Hom}(F_pC_ZB,C_TN)\xrightarrow{\eta_B^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}(C_TF_eB,C_TN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_eB,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(B,i^\times N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C_ZB,C_Zi^\times N).$$
Here the first arrow means precomposition by $\eta_B^{-1}$; the two full-faithfulness arrows are the unit identifications of the site-comparison theorem. This is the adjunction specified by the transported construction, within the domain of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Evaluating its inverse at $B=i^\times N$ and the identity gives its counit explicitly:
$$\mu^p_{C_TN}=C_T(\mu^e_N)\circ\eta_{i^\times N}.$$
For the projection map, use [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate] for the qcqs closed immersion $i$. Its displayed equation identifies the ordinary pullback/direct-image counits. The pullback-tensor isomorphism is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The projection transformation is the adjoint of the ordinary counit tensored with the second factor: after applying these two comparisons its transpose is $C_Z(\varepsilon^e_B\otimes1_{i^*M})$. This is also the transpose of the etale projection map after comparison, so uniqueness of adjunction identifies the two named projection transformations. Their inverses consequently agree; invertibility on our inputs is [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. Substituting this equality and the displayed formula for $\mu^p$ into the definition of $q$ in step 4 identifies $q^p_{C_TM,C_TN}$ with $C_Z(q^e_{M,N})$ under the named comparisons. To apply the revised statement of [lem-weil-finite-duality-site-comparison], first check its second-variable hypothesis. On either piece $W=T,Z$, the constant sheaf $A_W$ is constructible and has Tor interval $[0,0]$, since $A_W\otimes_A^LN=N$ for a degree-zero module sheaf $N$. Moreover $R\mathcal Hom_A(A_W,H)\cong H$: on the K-injective representative of step 3 the Hom complex from the ring sheaf is that representative itself. Hence $\omega_{W,\mathrm{et}}\cong D_WA_W$ is finite-Tor constructible, in particular bounded constructible, by [thm-fix-general-biduality]. Every first variable in the remaining duality comparisons is finite-Tor constructible: $L,K$ are inputs, their duals have this property by step 1, and $i^*K,P,U$ have it by step 2; further duals are again covered by step 1. Thus the lemma's canonical internal-Hom comparison applies with second variable $\omega_{W,\mathrm{et}}$. Write $w_W:C_W\omega_{W,\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{W,\mathrm{proet}}$ for its specified dualizing comparison and $\chi_{W,H}:C_WD_WH\xrightarrow{\sim}D_W^pC_WH$ for the induced duality comparison. The lemma states that, under the tensor identification,
$$\mathrm{ev}^{p}_{C_WH}\circ(\chi_{W,H}\otimes1)=w_W\circ C_W(\mathrm{ev}^{e}_H),$$
and that these comparisons identify the double-dual transposes. Its pro-etale exceptional functor is precisely the comparison-class transport already used here. These are comparisons of the named evaluation maps, not arbitrary object isomorphisms. Substitution in the displayed definitions of $r,b,c$ and their tensor-Hom transposes therefore identifies each with the comparison of its etale map. In particular the comparison of the equality in step 7 is $\beta^p=C_Z(D_Z(c_L)\delta_P)$, and that of step 8 is
$$\beta^p_{C_TD_TK}\circ i_p^*C_T\delta_K=D_Z^p(C_Z\alpha_K)\circ C_Z\delta_{i^*K}.$$
Thus the evaluation-defined pro-etale map is invertible and satisfies the required compatibility. This proves both clauses of the input on the chosen finite-stage categories.

split_report.summary: Kept the statement. Reused existing costalk duality, biduality, pullback preservation and generic ringed-site/category tools. Expanded the canonical-map identification and evaluation compatibility into explicit transpose equations; justified every finite-Tor domain and the pro-etale realization. The tagged Lean theorem covers only existence of an isomorphism, not the whole canonical-map statement. No new nodes. Second reading: corrected the etale D+ composition interface, separated preliminary and normalized costalk isomorphisms, and proved site-comparison counit/projection normalizations explicitly. Returned-delivery repair: revalidated every cited statement against the current DAG; expanded step 9 to check the revised finite-duality comparison coefficient scope, both argument hypotheses, transported exceptional convention and evaluation normalization, and refreshed its stale quotation. No item-statement change or new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: Steps 1--2 realize the first paragraph (preservation and alpha composed with Ri! delta); steps 3--8 realize the second paragraph with explicit q, r, b, beta=D(c)delta and the restricted-delta equation; step 9 makes the chosen finite-stage site realization precise.

tool_uses.why: Closed immersions are proper, providing the identity-open-part compactification used for the etale adjunction.
Exactness of constant-coefficient etale module pullback makes the etale restriction bounded before reflecting the Tor interval.
Etale constructibility of the ordinary closed restriction, so the pro-etale pullback lemma is not silently read as an etale statement.
Ambient etale adjunction for a closed immersion (compactification with identity open part); not an ambient pro-etale adjunction.
Generic adjunction-pasting with its counit normalization identifies Ri! omega_T with omega_Z.
Generic ringed-site resolution tool used to derive the actual tensor-Hom bijection, without assuming an O_X-specific theorem applies.
Generic small ringed-site K-injective existence used in the tensor-Hom deduction.
Generic K-flat/K-injective Hom-complex lemma (Stacks 0A96).
Generic ringed-site isomorphism of Hom complexes (Stacks 0A90), not its scheme-specialized consequences.
Generic ringed-site H^0(RHom)=Hom lemma (Stacks 08JA).
Finite-stage projection map, used only for a closed immersion and constructible finite-Tor tensor factor, to normalize q and alpha.
Generic fully faithful Yoneda embedding on the finite-Tor constructible category turns the written Hom chain into its unique comparison.
Generic site-comparison equivalence supplies etale-origin representatives for all the pro-etale inputs.
Generic ordinary restriction comparison fixes the same pullback in the two realizations.
Generic full faithfulness/unit comparison reduces the transported exceptional functor on etale-origin inputs.
Generic monoidal derived pullback comparison for the comparison morphism of ringed sites.
The counit-compatible restricted adjunction transports the etale map calculation without requiring a nonexistent global pro-etale ambient adjoint.
Finite-type schemes over the field are Noetherian, needed for the etale adjunctions; the unit supplies no geometric permanence lemma.
The open containing a locally closed piece is Noetherian and quasi-compact; generic geometric permanence.
The open factor of a locally closed piece is finite type; generic geometric permanence.
Provides actual compactifications of the structure morphisms needed for their etale adjoints.
Identifies the two left adjoints on the bounded-below comparison class and fixes the comparison used in the explicit counit formula.
Over Spec k bounds the dimension of the chosen finite-type compactification, checking the comparison-class adjunction hypothesis.
The etale D+ composition theorem, in the same coefficient category as the adjoints, replaces a citation of the pro-etale composition theorem.
Supplies the precise ordinary counit normalization needed to compare the named projection maps, beyond an existence-only direct-image comparison.
